title: Soft Tissue Sarcoma Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - the physician decides. Structural pathway for soft tissue sarcoma: presentation (extremity/trunk, retroperitoneal/intra-abdominal, advanced/metastatic) -> workup -> grade/size/depth risk stratification -> surgery +/- radiation +/- doxorubicin-based systemic therapy, with response-adapted restaging after neoadjuvant/induction therapy and margin-directed adjuvant therapy -> surveillance -> recurrence -> histology-directed advanced disease refined through line of therapy (first line -> on progression -> second line -> later line). Treatment leaves reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by id where one clinically fits; agents/modalities without a dose protocol are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. No proprietary guideline text is reproduced and no dose/regimen is invented. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the dose engine computes patient doses.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Soft Tissue Sarcoma; regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: Neoadjuvant/adjuvant radiation lowers local recurrence for high-grade or deep tumors and after close/positive margins; it does not clearly improve overall survival. Preoperative RT uses a smaller field/lower dose but has more acute wound complications than postoperative RT.

b.text: Perioperative doxorubicin-based chemotherapy in localized high-risk extremity/trunk sarcoma has an inconsistent survival benefit and is an individualized decision, weighed against anthracycline toxicity; favored for large (>5 cm), deep, high-grade tumors and chemosensitive histologies.

c.text: Retroperitoneal sarcoma is best treated by complete en-bloc resection of the tumor with adherent organs at a high-volume center; routine adjuvant chemotherapy is not standard and radiation is selective/investigational.

d.text: Surveillance intensity tracks grade: high-grade tumors need more frequent cross-sectional imaging of the primary site and chest (the lung is the dominant site of distant spread) than low-grade tumors.

e.text: For advanced/metastatic STS in a fit patient, doxorubicin-based therapy is the standard first-line backbone; a lifetime anthracycline cumulative-dose limit and baseline/serial cardiac function assessment apply, and the dose engine computes the patient dose.

f.text: Later-line and histology-specific agents (gemcitabine + docetaxel, trabectedin, pazopanib for non-adipocytic subtypes, eribulin for liposarcoma, taxanes for angiosarcoma, high-dose ifosfamide) are chosen by prior therapy and histology; several have no dedicated dose protocol here and are shown as guidance only.

nodes.name: Extremity workup
nodes.title: Extremity / trunk: workup
nodes.description: Image and biopsy before any resection so the tumor is staged and the biopsy tract can be excised en-bloc.
bullets: History and physical; measure tumor size and note depth relative to the investing fascia
MRI of the primary site with contrast (CT if MRI contraindicated)
Image-guided core-needle biopsy before resection; place the tract so it can be excised at surgery - avoid excisional biopsy of an undiagnosed mass
Expert sarcoma pathology review: histologic type, FNCLCC grade, margins
Chest CT to screen for pulmonary metastases; consider PET in selected cases
Multidisciplinary sarcoma-center referral before definitive treatment

nodes.name: Grade / size risk
nodes.title: Extremity / trunk: grade, size and resectability
nodes.description: Stratify by histologic grade, tumor size and depth, and whether a limb-sparing complete resection is feasible. This drives whether radiation and systemic therapy are added to surgery.

options.label: Locally advanced / not resectable with a functional limb

nodes.name: Low-risk extremity
nodes.title: Low-grade / small superficial: surgery
nodes.description: Wide local excision alone is usually sufficient; radiation only for margin concerns.
bullets: Wide local excision to negative margins (limb-sparing)
Adjuvant radiation generally not needed for small low-grade tumors resected with wide margins
Consider radiation for a positive margin that cannot be re-excised
No systemic therapy
Then surveillance

nodes.name: High-grade small
nodes.title: High-grade, small (<= 5 cm): surgery +/- RT
nodes.description: Limb-sparing wide excision with radiation added for close margins or deep high-grade tumors; routine chemotherapy is not indicated.
bullets: Limb-sparing wide local excision to negative margins
Adjuvant (or neoadjuvant) radiation for deep high-grade tumors or close/positive margins
Radiation may be omitted for a small high-grade tumor widely excised with a generous margin
Routine perioperative chemotherapy not indicated at this size
Then surveillance

nodes.name: Sequencing (large HG)
nodes.title: High-grade, large (> 5 cm): treatment sequencing
nodes.description: For large deep high-grade tumors, choose preoperative therapy (to shrink/facilitate limb-sparing surgery and treat micrometastatic risk) versus upfront resection.

options.label: Preoperative RT +/- doxorubicin-based chemo, then surgery
Upfront wide excision, then adjuvant therapy

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant response

options.label: Local progression or new distant metastases

nodes.name: Post-neoadjuvant surgery

nodes.name: Post-resection margin

nodes.name: Upfront R0

nodes.name: Still unresectable

Continue histology-directed systemic therapy for unresectable or metastatic disease
Palliative radiation for local symptoms

nodes.name: Retroperitoneal workup
nodes.title: Retroperitoneal / intra-abdominal: workup
nodes.description: Characterize the mass and its organ relationships before an operative plan; percutaneous biopsy is selective.
bullets: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast (+/- MRI) to map organ and vascular involvement
Image-guided core biopsy when it will change management (e.g. suspected lymphoma, germ-cell tumor, or planned preoperative therapy); a percutaneous coaxial approach is preferred
Expert pathology review - well-differentiated vs dedifferentiated liposarcoma and leiomyosarcoma are the common subtypes
Assess resectability and organs likely resected en-bloc; high-volume sarcoma center referral

nodes.name: RP resectability
nodes.title: Retroperitoneal: resectability
nodes.description: The single most important determinant of outcome is a complete en-bloc resection at the first operation.

nodes.name: RP sequencing
nodes.title: Retroperitoneal, resectable: sequencing
nodes.description: Choose upfront en-bloc resection versus a preoperative therapy trial (selective, e.g. for borderline resectability or on a protocol) before surgery.

nodes.name: RP en-bloc resection

nodes.description: Complete en-bloc resection with adherent organs; radiation selective, chemotherapy not standard.
bullets: Complete en-bloc resection of the tumor with involved/adherent organs, aiming for a macroscopically complete (R0/R1) resection at the first operation

nodes.name: RP preoperative therapy

nodes.name: RP preop response

nodes.name: RP resected after preop

Then surveillance

Transition to histology-directed systemic therapy
Palliative measures for obstruction / pain / bleeding as needed
